Offline npm consumers explicitly install local library/runtime tarballs with scripts disabled and no Cargo or driver override. Registry publication/acquisition, pnpm, Yarn and aliases remain open.
engineDevelopment.performanceStatus: The historical rebuilt-default comparison records median ratio 1.0672 (95% bootstrap interval 0.9919–1.1313), about 6.3% less complete-run time. Its confidence interval includes parity, so this final run does not establish a statistically resolved complete-run gain. The preceding identical-binary adoption comparisons show 5.3% less time against Playwright and 4.6% less time against residency off; all eighteen resident-on resource comparisons pass. The 10% complete-flow release target remains open. Failure medians and interaction/navigation observed maxima exceed the regression thresholds. The resource matrix remains bound to its pre-default binary; the assertion algorithm is unchanged. Native Linux performance, worker contention and broader release gates remain open. The current platform-package resolver and launch-budget changes have no new timing result.
engineDevelopment.sourceIdentity: The current native macOS/Bun development core passes 126 fresh groups at 501 unchanged source entries and driver b1923b63d24ddd31e4d7760edc1814952c4ce85d01ba5d785f64849a35ddeb6d. The same production passes 37 focused host groups and 36 shell/full-Chromium dialog/tracing/packed groups across Bun/Node22/Node24. The full core run's only delta from the focused source freeze is direct initialization in a protocol-version test. Older Linux runtime artifacts are historical and require rebuilding/verification for protocol 7; no new Linux or performance claim. See compatibility/evidence/dialog-recovery-checkpoint-2026-10-09.json.
engineDevelopment.residentResourceStatus: The preceding indexed-query binary passed all nine sustained-load CPU/memory/time gates at compatibility/evidence/resident-indexed-performance-checkpoint-2026-10-08.json. The evaluation-helper change leaves registry scheduling unchanged, but the older matrix is not a refreshed resource acceptance for the new binary.
engineDevelopment.binaryAttachmentsStatus: Protocol 5 keeps request-scoped raw/base64 application streams, 32 MiB decoded attachments, two active reservations and 64 KiB chunks. The Chromium JSON reader now admits typed response bodies beyond the ordinary 8 MiB reply/event cap. Its hard wire bound accounts for worst-case JSON escaping; it releases large frame buffers after use and ignores cancelled reply values. Complete oversized ordinary replies reject only their call. Fatal event/wire failures preserve their original error through page/context cleanup. Chromium JSON frames are still buffered, so this is not a constant-memory streaming CDP decoder.
engineDevelopment.browserPayloadStatus: At 179 matching source hashes, all 27 native macOS core groups and all 27 emulated Linux core groups pass, including 61 lifecycle cases per platform, with four focused Node22/headless-shell groups. Real-browser tests preserve a 9 MiB all-byte binary body and 2 MiB NUL text with a JSON representation above 12 MiB. Public response-body differentials match pinned Playwright byte-for-byte with one HTTP request per body. The initial Linux launch failed before creating a container because its local image was missing; rebuilding the pinned recipe restored the environment, and a separately recorded run passed. No new performance claim; native Linux and release gates remain open.
engineDevelopment.screenshotsStatus: All 29 native macOS core groups and all 29 emulated Linux core groups pass, including 57 Rust tests and 64 lifecycle cases per platform. Six focused Node22/headless-shell groups also pass. All 187 final source hashes match across this matrix. Child/parent rendering readiness makes image comparison independent of first-paint races shared by both engines. A blocked remote renderer times out and releases its temporary session without losing the parent. Screenshot differentials compare decoded pixels and dimensions, including navigation during fonts, natural viewport, unmodified cross-process frames and a 12.6 MB PNG. Per-page deadlines, exact preparation restoration, atomic files, payload limits and cancellation pass. Native window/screen metrics now match the pinned reference. No new performance claim; prior timings apply only to their recorded binaries.
engineDevelopment.pageErrorStatus: All 31 native macOS core groups pass, including 58 Rust tests and 65 lifecycle cases. Seven focused Node22/headless-shell groups and ten focused Linux amd64-emulation groups pass at the same 191 source hashes. The final three diagnostic differentials match all 20 error cases and nine lifecycle checks exactly against Playwright 1.60.0. Packed ESM/CommonJS consumers preserve Error inference, and oversized exceptions fail with ResourceLimitError and release owned resources. This is functional evidence only; a full current Linux core and native Linux/performance/release gates remain open.
engineDevelopment.handleStatus: All 33 native macOS core groups pass, including 62 Rust tests and 73 lifecycle cases. Ten focused Node22/headless-shell groups and thirteen focused Linux amd64-emulation groups pass at the same 199 source hashes. The three final handle differentials match nine shared groups, including ten primitive cases, and retain the S4.l BigInt difference separately. Seven native handle lifecycle/publication cases and all five caller-deadline allocation cases pass. Packed ESM/CommonJS consumers preserve nested handle inference, property types, DOM subtypes and frame evaluation. This is functional evidence only; full current Linux core, native Linux/performance and release gates remain open.
engineDevelopment.consoleStatus: All 35 native macOS core groups pass, including 65 Rust tests and 82 lifecycle cases. Sixteen focused Node22/headless-shell groups and nineteen focused Linux amd64-emulation groups pass at the same 205 source hashes. Console and handle differentials match their shared reference outcomes on all three configurations, with the S4.l BigInt difference retained separately. Eight native console cases cover ordering, ownership, long-task cleanup, clear invalidation, capacity and publication limits. Fresh packed ESM/CommonJS consumers preserve console callback inference and live handles. This is functional evidence only; full current Linux core, native Linux/performance and release gates remain open.
engineDevelopment.pageInitializationDecision: Parallel page initialization was tested and rejected: all 56 candidate verification groups passed, but the direct eight-pair comparison did not resolve complete-run or setup benefit. Complete-run ratio 0.9973 (95% interval 0.9767–1.0619); setup ratio 1.0195 (0.9732–1.0440). Navigation median point crossed the 5% regression threshold. Wrapper-inclusive process wall improved about 1.4%, but did not justify the added concurrency. Production initialization and optimized binary were restored exactly; the current 208-source tree passes 35 native groups, 65 Rust tests and 82 lifecycle cases. The candidate patch, every observation, separate attribution and verifier corruption checks are retained.
engineDevelopment.platformRuntimeStatus: Exact-version private platform packages now select the driver automatically, validate metadata and executable integrity before spawn, and preserve the ordinary launch budget. Clean offline npm ESM/CommonJS consumers run without install scripts, a driver override or Cargo. At 213 matching source hashes, 36 native macOS Node24 core groups, seven Node22/full-Chromium groups and ten emulated Linux groups pass; each platform runs the complete 82-case lifecycle suite. Package checks cover 23 macOS or 25 Linux cases, including corruption, unsupported libc, concurrent browsers and an expired lookup that cannot spawn. The selected Linux executable is built on glibc 2.31 and requires symbols through 2.30; its loader handshake passes on 2.31 and browser checks pass on Noble under emulation. The earlier glibc 2.39 artifact and its ten passing groups are retained separately. No publication, native Linux or packaged-startup performance claim.
